THE GLENLIVET

The first legally licensed distillery in the Livet Valley — and, since 1884, the only whisky permitted to bear the name “The” Glenlivet.

Explore The Collection Our Heritage
Scroll to Discover

In Gaelic, the name is said to mean “the smooth flowing one.” In 1824, George Smith rode to Elgin to claim the first legal distiller’s licence in the parish of Glenlivet — a decision that made him enemies among the valley’s smugglers, and made his whisky the standard by which Speyside would come to be known.

George & J. G. Smith  —  The Glenlivet Distillery, Banffshire
Since 1824

A Legacy Forged in the Livet Valley

Two centuries of a single, unbroken pursuit — begun by one man's refusal to distil in the shadows.

1822

A King Requests a Dram

King George IV, visiting Scotland, asked for a taste of the already-famed Glenlivet whisky — distilled illegally, deep in the isolated Livet valley, by a farmer named George Smith.

1823–24

The First Legal Licence

Following the Excise Act of 1823, George Smith rode to Elgin and became the first man in the parish of Glenlivet to hold a legal distiller’s licence — a decision that set him apart from every illicit still in the glen.

1824

Pistols at the Ready

Neighbouring smugglers, furious at his legitimacy, threatened to burn his distillery to the ground. George Smith carried a pair of flintlock pistols at all times, making clear he would not be moved.

1871

A Son Takes the Reins

On George Smith’s death, his youngest son, John Gordon Smith, left his legal training behind to continue his father’s life’s work at the distillery.

1884

The Right to “The”

As rival distilleries across Speyside appended “Glenlivet” to their own names, the Smith family fought a landmark legal case. The ruling was final: only one distillery would ever be permitted to call itself “The” Glenlivet.

2024

Two Hundred Years

The Glenlivet marked two centuries since its licence was first granted — celebrating the milestone with the release of its oldest expression to date.

The Craft

An Uncommonly Gentle Spirit

Every element of The Glenlivet's craft was chosen to produce one thing: a lighter, more fruit-forward single malt than Speyside had seen before.

I.

Josie's Well

Water drawn from Josie's Well and the Blairfindy Well — soft, mineral-rich sources that have fed the distillery since the nineteenth century.

II.

The Lantern Stills

Fourteen copper pot stills, tall and lantern-shaped to George Smith's own design, allowing only the lightest, most aromatic vapours to pass through.

III.

The House Style

The result is the floral, fruit-driven character — orchard fruit, pineapple, pear, soft vanilla — that came to define the Speyside style itself.

For decades, that character was shaped by Master Distiller Alan Winchester. Today it is carried forward under the guardianship of The Glenlivet's Cask Master, Kevin Balmforth, and his team.

The Collection

Six Portraits of a Single Malt

Each expression of The Glenlivet carries its own story of cask, time, and character.

12 Year Old
George Smith's Gold
The Glenlivet 12 Year Old

Double oak matured across European and American casks, the 12 Year Old is the heart of The Glenlivet's signature style — banana and pineapple, peaches and pears, vanilla and toffee, finishing smooth, gentle and long.

40 Year Old
The Forty Year Watch
The Glenlivet 40 Year Old

The distillery's oldest permanent expression, matured over four decades and finished in custom Jerez casks seasoned with Oloroso and Pedro Ximénez sherry. Bottled at cask strength, with notes of poached plum, charred orange and warming spice.

Founder's Reserve
The Founder's Hand
The Glenlivet Founder's Reserve

A tribute to George Smith himself, matured in traditional oak and first-fill American oak casks and distilled through the same lantern-shaped stills he designed nearly two centuries ago — smooth, creamy and fruit-forward.

12 Year Old
Breaking The Old Walls
The Glenlivet 12 Year Old

A nod to 1824, when one man's decision to distil in the open broke two hundred years of hidden tradition in the Livet Valley — and let The Glenlivet's character finally see the light.

15 Year Old
The Limousin Inheritance
The Glenlivet 15 Year Old — French Oak Reserve

Finished in French Limousin oak casks of the kind traditionally used for Cognac — a deliberate departure that lends this expression its rich, spiced, distinctly continental character.

15 Year Old
The Gilded Pour
The Glenlivet 15 Year Old — French Oak Reserve

Every cask in the French Oak Reserve is hand-selected before finishing — a deliberate, unhurried process, true to a distillery that has never rushed its whisky.

In Conversation

Questions of Heritage

Answers drawn directly from The Glenlivet's own history and record.

Q. Why is it called “The” Glenlivet?

Because in 1884, after years of rival distilleries appending “Glenlivet” to their own names, a landmark ruling granted George Smith's family the sole right to the definite article. Every other producer could only hyphenate — theirs alone could be “The” Glenlivet.

Q. What gives it that fruity character?

The tall, narrow, lantern-shaped copper stills, designed by George Smith himself, permit only the lightest vapours through — producing the floral, orchard-fruit style now considered the Speyside signature.

Q. Who shapes The Glenlivet today?

Cask Master Kevin Balmforth and his team continue the work once led by Master Distiller Alan Winchester, selecting and finishing casks in pursuit of the same character George Smith first envisioned in 1824.

Q. Why French oak at all?

The French Oak Reserve is matured in Limousin oak casks — the same variety long used for Cognac — a deliberate experiment that gives the 15 Year Old its distinctive spice and depth.

FAQ

Good to Know

— Where is The Glenlivet made?

At The Glenlivet Distillery in Ballindalloch, Moray — in the heart of Speyside, Scotland, on the site George Smith first licensed in 1824.

— What is the house style?

Light, floral and fruit-forward — orchard fruit, citrus, vanilla and soft oak — the defining profile of the Speyside style that The Glenlivet helped establish.

— How should it be enjoyed?

Neat, on the rocks, or in a considered cocktail — The Glenlivet's balance and smoothness were built to be versatile, from the 12 Year Old to the rarest editions in the range.

— Is The Glenlivet still family-founded?

The distillery was founded and run by the Smith family from 1824 through successive generations. It is today part of Chivas Brothers, within the Pernod Ricard group, while continuing to distil on its original Speyside site.
